cnalysis.name: CNalysis (now State Navigate)
cnalysis.notes: cnalysis.com redirects to State Navigate, a nonprofit whose 2026 forecasts cover state legislatures and governors only. Found no 2026 U.S. House district forecast (no probabilities or ratings) from CNalysis/State Navigate.

ddhq.name: Decision Desk HQ / The Hill
ddhq.final_date: 2026-11-02 15:03:59.945696 UTC (page: 'Last Updated: Monday, November 2 at 10:03 AM EST')
ddhq.notes: House seats figure is DDHQ's projected seat count (labelled 'House Seats Projections'), not explicitly a median. District win probabilities published to 2 decimals, margins as whole points (D margin as attached to the D party). Model blends polls, prediction markets (~25% weight) and fundamentals. votes.decisiondeskhq.com is behind a Vercel bot checkpoint; The Hill mirror page was used. Secondary: Newsweek reports the same final 84% / 241-194; DDHQ's Oct 26 Substack cited 79%. 270toWin mirrors DDHQ only as categorical ratings (Nov 2 15:21 UTC).

economist.name: The Economist
economist.notes: Final update 2026-11-03 (timestamp.json 1793690435 = 07:20 UTC), days_before_vote=0. margin = (2*avg_dem_2_party_vote_share-1)*100, i.e. two-party margin derived from published mean share. low/high_dem_conf interval bounds left in the raw CSV. IN-1: Economist lists R candidate Sparks-Wade, not Regnitz (name_match false); SC-5 spelled Ditmer. Page text (wayback 2026-11-04 01:06 UTC) confirms 93% and average 234-201.

fiftyplusone.name: FiftyPlusOne (G. Elliott Morris model; also published via Strength In Numbers)
fiftyplusone.notes: Live page still served the final model run (model_date 2026-11-03, timestamp 2026-11-03T05:53:08Z) on 2026-11-11. p_win per candidate from model; margin = D median share minus R median share.

kalshi.name: Kalshi
kalshi.notes: p_dem = midpoint of yes bid/ask at close of the hourly candle ending 2026-11-03T12:00Z (7am ET) for the Dem market; bid/ask/last trade kept. Only ~60 of 152 districts had Kalshi markets (series HOUSE<ST><N> / KXHOUSE<ST><N>). House control from CONTROLH-2026-D. Seat median not recorded. ME-2 market (HOUSEME2-26) had not settled as of download.

polymarket.name: Polymarket
polymarket.notes: Prices = last hourly prices-history point at or before 2026-11-03T12:00Z (7am ET), Dem-YES token of '<ST>-<NN> House Election Winner' events (ME-02 and CA-22 use differently named slugs). House control: 'Which party will win the House in 2026?' Dem YES at 2026-11-03T11:00Z. Seat median not recorded (only bracket markets exist). p_rep stored for reference; p_dem+p_rep may not sum to 1.

rtwh.name: Race to the WH (Logan Phillips)
rtwh.final_date: 2026-11-03 (sheet stamp: Last Updated on Nov 3, 2:36 PM ET)
rtwh.notes: District P(win) and projected lead from the Infogram live-data feed behind the RTWH House page (fetched 2026-11-11). Every one of the 152 districts' Win Trend series ends at "Nov 3" and equals the Projection By Race value, so these are the final pre-election numbers. National toplines in the same feed (Dem 96.2% chance, 236.5 projected seats) sit next to a stale stamp "Last Updated on Sep 26" and are inconsistent with the Nov 3 district probabilities (which sum to 232.4 expected Dem seats), so they are not recorded as final. AK-AL: p_dem is for Bill Hill (I). Margins are RTWH projected lead in points, + = Dem.

silver.name: Silver Bulletin (Nate Silver / Eli McKown-Dawson, FLIPR)

house_p_dem_secondary.source: Newsweek, 'Who Will Win the Midterms? What Polls Show 3 Days Out'

silver.notes: FLIPR published race-by-race House forecasts (final update 2026-11-03, post_date 2026-11-03T05:16Z), but the district table and topline are behind the Substack paywall ('audience: only_paid'); the free code embeds on the pages only carry polling averages (public Google Sheet CSVs), not model output. No public CSV/JSON, GitHub repo or 270toWin mirror found. Final-day free text says only that a Democratic House majority 'looks all but certain' (no number). Latest secondary topline: 95.1% D, avg 240 D seats (Oct 29, Newsweek, unverified); earlier Oct 8: 93.1%, avg 238.7. Newsweek also reported (Oct 8, not final) TX-23 R +0.2 and TX-15/23/35 as tossups; not included as final values. No district values recorded.

sin.name: Strength In Numbers (G. Elliott Morris)
sin.notes: Not a separate model: Morris's forecast is the FiftyPlusOne model (he runs 50+1's forecasts; SIN republishes it). Use the 'fiftyplusone' entry for district odds. Final SIN post (Nov 3) says the model gives Democrats 'a roughly 8-in-10 chance of winning majorities in both chambers'; Political Wire (Nov 3) quotes Morris: 'I give the Democrats a 99-in-100 chance of taking 218 seats or more' (50+1 final data shows p_win 0.9826).

splitticket.name: Split Ticket (published by The Argument)
splitticket.notes: Win probabilities published as whole percents; margins as published (D positive). Datawrapper charts last modified 2026-11-03 ~04:07Z, before polls opened. AK-AL D slot is independent Bill Hill.

votehub.name: VoteHub
votehub.notes: VoteHub published a district-level House forecast, but votehub.com returns 403 to non-browser clients and its robots.txt/page footer prohibit scraping or automated collection without written permission, so no district numbers were collected. Topline 84% (last updated Oct 14) is from Newsweek, unverified; no final (Nov 2-3) figure found. Newsweek says VoteHub favored Democrats in AZ-1, IA-1, NE-2, MI-10 (Hines), PA-7, PA-10, OH-7 (Poindexter), UT (McAdams) among 15 Trump-won seats -- direction only, no probabilities.
